# Getting Inrix data

Data was scraped from this link: https://inrix.com/scorecard/ Codes are hosted on github repo: thuy2020/inrix_scraping

```{r}
#Scraped from this link, hosted on github repo thuy2020/inrix_scraping: https://inrix.com/scorecard/
inrix <- read_csv("data/2022/delay_hour_2022_US_urban_area.csv") %>% 
         mutate(state.abb = str_extract(urban_area, ".{2}$"),
                city = str_replace(urban_area, ".{2}$", ""),
                city = str_replace_all(city, "City", ""),
      
                city = str_squish(city)) %>% 
        select(-c(`...1`, urban_area)) %>% 
  left_join(df)


inrix 

```

Count number of cities collected in IRIX by state

```{r}
inrix %>% add_count(state.name) %>% 
  arrange(desc(n)) %>% select(state.name, n) %>% 
  distinct(state.name)
```

Simple sum of delayed hour by state in INRIX

```{r}
inrix %>% group_by(state.name) %>% 
  summarise(total_delayed_hour_by_state = sum(delay_2022)) %>% arrange(desc(total_delayed_hour_by_state))
```

INRIX only provides delay hours for 295 US cities. Our goal is to use this data to extrapolate delay hours for more metro areas, and subsequently all states.

Our assumption is that delay hours is highly correlated with the number of auto commuters. In the next steps, we will:

-   get the auto commuters data for metro areas from ACS
-   quantify the relationship between the number of auto commuters and delay hours by running a simple linear model
-   lastly, we use the coefficient from the model above to predict delay hours for other metro areas whose cities are not covered by INRIX.

# Commuter data ACS

Table S0802: Means of transportation to work by selected characteristics. https://data.census.gov/table/ACSST5Y2022.S0802?g=010XX00US\$31000M1

This dataset contains 392 cities. It has `auto_commuters_alone`, `auto_commuters_carpooled`. We use these to calculate auto_commuters_combined, in which: auto_commuters_combined = auto_commuters_alone + auto_commuters_carpooled/2.2 (factor 2.2 is the average carpool occupancy).

```{r}
commuter_data <- import("data/2022/ACSST1Y2022.S0802-Data.csv") %>% 
  select(V2, V205, V407) %>% 
  rename(city = 1, 
         auto_commuters_alone = 2,
         auto_commuters_carpooled = 3) %>% slice(-c(1:2)) %>% 
  # matches any character (.) any number of times (*), followed by a comma and optional whitespace (\\s*)
  mutate(state.name = sub(".*,\\s*", "", city), 
         #state = sub("Metro Area", "", state),
         city = sub(",.*", "", city), 
         city = sub("(city)|(City)|(municipality)|(town)|(CDP)", "", city),
         city = str_squish(city)) 
  #filter(state.name %in% df$state.name) 
  
```

```{r}
acs_inrix <- commuter_data %>% 
  left_join(inrix) %>% 
  filter(state.name %in% df$state.name) %>% 
  mutate(auto_commuters_combined = as.numeric(auto_commuters_alone) + as.numeric(auto_commuters_carpooled)/2.2)

#acs_inrix has 646 observations, of which 191 have full data. Predict delay by auto commuters

model <- lm(delay_2022 ~ auto_commuters_combined, data = acs_inrix)  

#Check model
summary(model)
```

The model predicts that for each increase of 10,000 auto commuters, a city's delay hours is expected to increase by .284 hour.

```{r}
#Use the model to predict the congestion hours for areas not included in the inrix data set
 acs_inrix %>% 
 # filter(is.na(delay_hours)) %>% 
  add_predictions(model) 
  mutate(delay_hours = pred) %>% 
  select(-pred)

```

```{r}
#Clean data
commuter_data_clean <- commuter_data %>% 
  mutate(auto_commuters_alone = as.numeric(auto_commuters_alone),
         auto_commuters_carpooled = as.numeric(auto_commuters_carpooled),
         auto_commuters_combined = auto_commuters_alone + auto_commuters_carpooled/2.2) %>%    #2.2 is the average carpool occupancy. 
  filter(!is.na(auto_commuters_alone)) %>%  
  mutate(city = str_replace(area, ",.*", ""),       #remove state name and area label (metro vs micro)
         city = str_replace(city, " City", ""),     #remove "City" in city names 
         first_city = str_split(city, "-", simplify = T)[,1],
         # city = str_replace(city, "-.*", ""),   #retain the first city name only
         second_city = str_split(city, "-", simplify = T)[,2],
         third_city = str_split(city, "-", simplify = T)[,3],
         
         first_state = str_extract(area, ", .."),   
         first_state = str_replace(first_state, ", ", ""),  
         urban = ifelse(grepl("Metro Area", area), "Metro Area", "Micro Area")
         ) %>%
  filter(urban == "Metro Area") %>%   #retain metro areas only. 
  relocate(area, city, first_city, second_city, third_city, first_state, urban) %>% 
  mutate(across(where(is.character), str_trim))

commuter_data_clean %>% select(-c(auto_commuters_alone, auto_commuters_carpooled, urban)) %>% datatable()
```

ACS does not provide number of auto commuters by city. Instead, auto commuters are counted by metro area, which may consist of one, two or three cities across states.

On the other hand, IRIX provides data by city. We average the INRIX values and attribute it to the whole metro erea.

For example, Albany-Schenectady-Troy, NY Metro Area has 336582.09 auto commuters. INRIX has delay hours for Albany (11) and Schenectady (20). Hence, delay hours for the whole Albany-Schenectady-Troy, NY Metro Area is 15.5 hours.

# Combine commuter data (ACS) and Inrix data

```{r}
congestion_data <- commuter_data_clean %>% 
  left_join(inrix, by = c("first_state" = "state", "first_city" = "city")) %>% 
  left_join(inrix, by = c("first_state" = "state", "second_city" = "city")) %>% 
  left_join(inrix, by = c("first_state" = "state", "third_city" = "city")) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(delay_hours = mean(c(delay_2022.x, delay_2022.y, delay_2022), na.rm = T)) %>% 
  ungroup()

congestion_data %>% 
  select(c(area, city, first_city, second_city, first_state, delay_hours)) %>% 
  drop_na() %>% 
  datatable()
```

Out of 392 metro areas in ACS commuter data, we can only get delay hours data for 189 areas. The rest needs to be predicted.

```{r}
#Run a linear regression model to find the relationship between congestion hours (inrix data) 
#and the number of auto commuters
congestion_data_inrix <- congestion_data %>% 
  filter(!is.na(delay_hours))

model <- lm(delay_hours ~ auto_commuters_combined, data = congestion_data_inrix)  

#Check model
summary(model)
```

The model predicts that for each increase of 10,000 auto commuters, a city's delay hours is expected to increase by .284 hour.

```{r}
#Use the model to predict the congestion hours for areas not included in the inrix data set
congestion_data_non_inrix <- congestion_data %>% 
  filter(is.na(delay_hours)) %>% 
  add_predictions(model) %>% 
  mutate(delay_hours = pred) %>% 
  select(-pred)

congestion_data_non_inrix
```

```{r}
# combine
congestion_data_inrix_noninrix <- bind_rows(congestion_data_inrix, congestion_data_non_inrix) %>% 
  arrange(area)
```

# Vehicle miles data

```{r}
vehicle_miles_data <- read_excel("data/2022/hm74.xls", sheet = "A", skip = 12) %>% 
  select(1, 2, 3, 9, 15, 21, 27) %>% 
  rename(area = 1,
         state = 2, 
         unreported = 3, 
         interstate_total = 4, 
         ofe_total = 5,
         opa_total = 6, 
         ma_total = 7) %>% 
  slice(-(1:1))

vehicle_miles_data_clean <- vehicle_miles_data %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  
  mutate(first_city = str_replace(area, ",.*",""),
         first_city = str_replace(first_city, "-.*",""),
         first_city = str_replace(first_city, " City", ""),
         first_state = str_extract(area, ", .."),
         first_state = str_replace(first_state, ", ", "")) %>% 
  
  mutate(across(.cols = 3:7, .fns = as.numeric),
         # total daily mile traveled 
         total_dmvt = interstate_total + ofe_total + opa_total + ma_total) %>%    
         #exclude "unreported" dvm based on the documentation and past results. 
         #Can change this later if we decide to include this number. 
   
  group_by(area) %>% 
  ## the percent shared for each state in cases where a city counted in 2 states. 
  #Eg. Augusta-Richmond County, GA--SC -->  GA =  .73, SC = .27
  mutate(dmvt_pct = total_dmvt/sum(total_dmvt)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(area, first_city,  first_state, state, dmvt_pct)
```

```{r}
#Combine inrix and non-inrix congestion data and add the daily vehicle miles traveled data 
#to allocate the commuter number for multi-state areas
delay_data_final <- congestion_data_inrix_noninrix  %>% 
  left_join(vehicle_miles_data_clean, by = c("first_city", "first_state")) %>%
  mutate(dmvt_pct = ifelse(is.na(dmvt_pct), 1, dmvt_pct),
         state = ifelse(is.na(state), first_state, state),
         total_delay_hours = delay_hours * auto_commuters_combined * dmvt_pct,
         adjusted_auto_commuters_combined = auto_commuters_combined * dmvt_pct)

#Calculate congestion hours per commuter by state
df_state = data.frame(state.abb, state.name) %>% 
  add_row(state.abb = c("DC", "PR"),
          state.name = c("District of Columbia", "Puerto Rico"))

delay_data_summary <- delay_data_final %>% 
  group_by(state) %>% 
  summarise(state_tot_delay_hours = sum(total_delay_hours),
            state_tot_commuters = sum(adjusted_auto_commuters_combined)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  left_join(df_state, by = c("state" = "state.abb")) %>% 
  select(-state) %>% 
  rename(state = state.name) 
  # mutate(state_avg_delay_hours = state_tot_delay_hours/state_tot_commuters)

```
